question: Dependency Graphs: How does FastAPI construct and resolve sub-dependencies in a request dependency graph?

options.text: FastAPI builds a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) of dependencies, evaluating shared sub-dependencies once per request (unless usecache=False is set) and injecting resolved values into dependent functions.
FastAPI re-evaluates every dependency function from scratch on each sub-dependency reference within a single request, even when use_cache=True, to guarantee freshness.

FastAPI resolves dependencies in the exact reverse order they are declared in the function signature, and shared sub-dependencies are always instantiated once per sub-dependency reference, never shared.
Dependencies are resolved lazily only when their return value is actually used inside the route body; unused Depends() declarations are silently skipped and never invoked at all.

explanation: Specification answer: FastAPI builds a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) of dependencies, evaluating shared sub-dependencies once per request (unless usecache=False is set) and injecting resolved values into dependent functions.

question: Yield Lifecycle: What exact moments in request execution correspond to code before vs after the yield statement in a dependency?

options.text: - Code before yield: Executes during request setup before the route handler is invoked. - Code after yield: Executes during response teardown after the route handler finishes, even if an unhandled error occurred.
Code before yield runs during response teardown, and code after yield runs during request setup -- the two phases are reversed from their actual timing.
Code before and after yield both run during request setup, back to back, before the route handler is ever invoked; the split only matters for readability, not execution timing.
Code after yield only executes if the route handler explicitly calls request.state.cleanup(); if that call is omitted, the teardown code after yield is skipped entirely.

explanation: Specification answer: - Code before yield: Executes during request setup before the route handler is invoked. - Code after yield: Executes during response teardown after the route handler finishes, even if an unhandled error occurred.

question: ASGI Middleware Pipeline: Describe the journey of an HTTP request through custom ASGI middleware to the route endpoint and back.

options.text: Incoming bytes pass through each middleware layer in outer-to-inner order, execute the endpoint, and the resulting Response flows back through the layers in reverse (inner-to-outer) order.
Incoming bytes pass through each middleware layer in inner-to-outer order first, execute the endpoint, and the Response skips all middleware entirely on the way back out.

Middleware only wraps the Response after the endpoint executes; incoming requests bypass all middleware layers and reach the route handler directly and immediately.

explanation: Specification answer: Incoming bytes pass through each middleware layer in outer-to-inner order, execute the endpoint, and the resulting Response flows back through the layers in reverse (inner-to-outer) order.

What is the verified root cause?
